title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（髙橋元貴研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Takahashi Genki)
educationalGoal: Through field survey and analysis of documents and pictorial old maps, we will clarify the principles of city and settlement formation, spatial organization, spatial transformation from a historical approach. The course will also explore the future of cities and settlements in the form of design and research. Students are expected to set their own specific themes and research fields, and conduct the necessary research to carry them out. The results will be compiled as a research paper or a design work.
advice:
In this course, we will cover the following materials:
1) problem findings concerning urban spaces, regional or local areas, and surrounding social conditions
2) analysis of the structure of problems
3) design of research methods
4) implementation (accomplishment of a project)
5) presentation (by graduation thesis or a design work)
requiredKnowledge: No special knowledge nor skills are necessary.

activityGoals.body: be able to collect data, analyze the structure of the problems, and explain the social needs of a project.
be able to design appropriate methods to achieve the goal and accomplish a project by yourself
be able to make a clear and meaningful visual presentation to others
be able to explain all the processes of a project logically and complete a project (paper/work)
be able to understand social trends and decide what to do after graduation

1) explain the social needs of a project, based on collected empirical data, results of analysis of problem structure.
2) design appropriate processes or appropriate methods of research activity to achieve the goal and accomplish the project logically and as scheduled
3) complete a project and make a clear, meaningful, and attractive visual presentation to others
achievementLevels.standard:
1) explain the needs of a project based on empirical data.
2) design processes or methods of a project and accomplish it
3) complete a project as scheduled and make a clear and meaningful presentation to others

              Through field survey and analysis of documents and pictorial old maps, we will clarify the principles of city and settlement formation, spatial organization, spatial transformation from a historical approach. The course will also explore the future of cities and settlements in the form of design and research. Students are expected to set their own specific themes and research fields, and conduct the necessary research to carry them out. The results will be compiled as a research paper or a design work.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In this course, we will cover the following materials:
1) problem findings concerning urban spaces, regional or local areas, and surrounding social conditions
2) analysis of the structure of problems
3) design of research methods
4) implementation (accomplishment of a project)
5) presentation (by graduation thesis or a design work)
